item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Aug. 2, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona, Republican Rep. Mike Turner of Ohio and Independent former Sen. Joe Manchin of West Virginia.

item.title: U.S., Israel preparing to bombard energy-related targets in Iran, sources say
item.description: The U.S. and Israel plan to hit Iran's energy infrastructure as soon as this weekend, although no final decision has been made, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: U.S. and Israel preparing to strike energy-related targets in Iran, sources say
item.description: CBS News has learned from sources familiar that President Trump is considering a coordinated strike with Israel on Iranian energy targets as soon as this weekend, but a final decision is pending. CBS News' Nancy Cordes and Samantha Vinograd have the latest.

item.title: Brother of slain cartel leader "El Mencho" pleads guilty to U.S. drug charges
item.description: Antonio Oseguera Cervantes worked for cartels with his brother Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes, the drug lord known as "El Mencho​," according to federal prosecutors.

item.title: U.S. preparing new Iran strikes as Trump says "We've done an amazing job"
item.description: There was no sign of the conflict ending as Iran claimed to have struck two ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: New York sues Kalshi, alleging it enables illegal gambling
item.description: A growing number of U.S. states are seeking to crack down on prediction markets, but face pushback from federal regulators.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie ransom notes are released, including message saying she died
item.description: One of the notes threatened to kill Nancy Guthrie if a multimillion-dollar ransom wasn't paid in a week. The second, a few days later, says, "She is buried in nature now."

item.title: Los Angeles falls behind other California cities in rollout of speed cameras
item.description: The delay comes as speeding remains a leading factor in traffic crashes across California.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial: Patrick Clancy takes the stand | Case by Case
item.description: Three years after the deaths of Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy, the trial of their mother Lindsay is underway. This week, CBS News legal analyst Caroline Polisi and CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul take listeners inside the courtroom for jury selection, opening statements, and the highly anticipated testimony of her now ex-husband Patrick Clancy. They examine the prosecution's claim that Lindsay Clancy carefully planned the killings and the defense's contention that postpartum psychosis left her unable to control her actions.

item.title: F-35 fighter jet crashes near San Diego Marine Corps base, sparking fire
item.description: An aerial photo shows a smoking F-35 fighter jet next to scorched vegetation in a field at Marine Corps Air Station Miramar.

item.title: Scary video shows European fires that have displaced over 250,000 in France, Spain and beyond
item.description: At least one person has died, and more than 250,000 have been forced to flee their homes as wildfires ravage Western Europe in July, spreading across France, Spain, Greece, and the United Kingdom.

item.title: Rare footage of humpback whale birth captured on drone video
item.description: The footage is believed to be only the fourth complete humpback whale birth ever recorded on film anywhere in the world and the first-ever captured by drone.

item.title: Drone captures humpback whale birth for first time
item.description: A photographer operating a drone off the coast of Australia captured a humpback whale giving birth. It's believed to be the first time such a birth has been recorded by a drone.

item.title: Spain sends over 25,000 migrants back to Morocco from Ceuta; dozens dead
item.description: The president of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, estimated that 60,000 migrants had entered the enclave from Morocco and said that at least 34 people had died.

item.title: 3 mortgage rate mistakes to avoid post-Fed rate pause
item.description: A Fed rate pause doesn't need to be magnified by borrowers as long as they avoid making these three timely mistakes.

item.title: New York sues Kalshi over alleged illegal gambling
item.description: New York State is suing Kalshi, the online betting portal, for allegedly operating an illegal gambling business. Kalshi says that it is a federally regulated exchange and is not subject to state laws. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: Watch: F-35 crash at Marine Corps station in San Diego
item.description: An F-35 military aircraft appears to have crashed near the Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in San Diego, California. There is no word yet from authorities on what caused the crash or any possible injuries.

item.title: Families sue Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube over deaths of 4 teens
item.description: The families of four children who died by suicide allege that using social media led to depression, anxiety and other mental health problems.

item.title: Here's how much interest a $10,000 2-year CD account will earn if opened this August
item.description: In today's economy, locking $10,000 into a 2-year CD makes sense. Here's how much interest you would earn if you do.

item.title: Doctors testify in Lindsay Clancy trial, jury views home where 3 kids were killed
item.description: Day 4 of the Lindsay Clancy murder trial started with a jury visit to her former Duxbury, Massachusetts home where her three kids were killed.

item.title: 3 states would face Colorado River water cuts under federal plan
item.description: Arizona, California, and Nevada would take less water from the Colorado River under a federal proposal to stave off a crisis in the river.

item.title: Netflix sued for allegedly losing unreleased Nicolas Cage movie
item.description: A lawsuit alleges that a drive storing a $45 million spy film starring Nicolas Cage was "stolen right off a Netflix desk."

item.title: U.S. probing if Iran was behind cyberattack on water systems in 7 states
item.description: Malicious cyber activity affected technology at water systems in at least seven states this week, including Minnesota, leading authorities to dig into whether Iranian actors are behind the attack, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Tony Romo on leave from CBS Sports after arrest
item.description: Romo was arrested in Wisconsin last week, accused of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

item.title: Democrats demand training info on ICE agent who killed immigrant in Maine
item.description: Two Democrats are demanding details and records about the training of an ICE officer who shot and killed a Colombian immigrant in Maine, according to a letter obtained by CBS News.

item.title: OCTROT heated blankets and throws recalled after fires and injuries
item.description: Chinese-made electric bedding poses "risk of serious injury or death," according to U.S. product safety regulators.

item.title: FIFA official resigns in protest of World Cup investment plan
item.description: The pressure is rising on FIFA President Gianni Infantino to ditch a $20 billion privatization plan, but soccer's governing body is doubling down and criticizing the media.

item.title: Famed climber among 10 missing on Pakistan peak; 4 bodies recovered
item.description: Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing on Pakistan's Broad Peak located four bodies and were looking for the others, officials said. Acclaimed climber Nirmal Purja was among the missing.

item.title: Trump says Hamas agreed to next phase of Gaza peace deal, including disarmament
item.description: President Trump said Hamas and his international "Board of Peace" have agreed on the next steps in a peace deal that includes Hamas' disarmament in the Gaza Strip.

item.title: Inside a California data center as communities raise concerns about energy costs
item.description: California lawmakers are considering several proposals affecting data centers, including bills intended to shield utility customers from increased electricity costs.
